To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the vertical migration of cod larvae in relation to light intensity and prey availability is a necessary part of the larval life cycle, 2) the vertical distribution of cod eggs and larvae is influenced by environmental factors, 3) the distribution of cod eggs is influenced by the physical characteristics of water, and 4) cod larvae migrate from the depths where they hatch to the upper photic layer when feeding
the vertical distribution of cod larva is influenced by ontogenetic changes, by prey availability, and by the physical characteristics of water column.
the vertical distribution of cod eggs and larvae is determined by a combination of physical and biological factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the physical environment in determining the vertical distribution and feeding conditions for Baltic Sea cod larvae.
the vertical distribution of cod eggs and larvae in the Baltic Sea.
the vertical distribution of Baltic cod larvae in relation to their feeding ecology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cod larvae in the Baltic are neutrally buoyent at hatching.
the vertical distribution of cod in the Baltic Sea is determined by a combination of ontogenetic and environmental factors.
the vertical migration of cod larvae in Bornholm Basin is mainly driven by the need of feeding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Baltic Sea is an extreme habitat for larval fishes, and the vertical distribution of cod is determined by a number of factors that are not found in other regions.
the vertical migration of cod larvae in this area is a consequence of a combination of environmental and ontogenetic factors.
the vertical distribution of cod eggs and larvae in the Baltic Sea is determined by a complex interaction of environmental conditions and larval behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the vertical distribution of cod eggs and larvae is determined by their physical characteristics (buoyancy) and their feeding behavior, which is in turn influenced by the availability of food and the light regime.
cod larvae in the Baltic must swim actively to locate suitable prey and to avoid low oxygen conditions.
the vertical distribution of cod eggs and larvae in the Baltic is strongly influenced by the hydrography of the basin.
